title: Role-adjusted GM pitcher-acquisition ranking (Option B confound control)
method: modeling/role_adjustment.py — partial deployment change (bf_delta innings + lev_delta leverage) out of player-level pitcher war_delta via OLS residual, then aggregate raw vs role-adjusted by receiver GM.
scope_and_caveats: PITCHER acquisitions only (player-level war_delta with pre/post deployment), n=910-933 legs — NOT the full dollar-surplus GM ranking.
Explanatory/post-hoc only: deployment deltas use the post-trade season (t+1), so this is attribution, not prediction (would be leakage as a forecasting feature).
Per-GM n is small (15-32 pitcher acquisitions). Individual GM moves are DIRECTIONAL, not definitive — same small-sample caveat as the original GM ranking's r=0.27 within-GM persistence.
WAR mechanically rewards leverage (gmLI), so partialling out lev_delta removes that mechanical credit by design — which is the point.

ranking_movement.interpretation: Ranking is mostly stable but meaningfully reordered — ~32% of rank variance reshuffles once role inflation is removed.

takeaway: When you stop crediting GMs for the role they assign (innings + leverage) and score only the skill-attributable residual of acquired-pitcher WAR, the pitcher-acquisition leaderboard reshuffles meaningfully. GMs whose acquired pitchers' raw WAR was propped up by heavy usage drop; GMs who held performance on lighter usage rise. Directional at the individual level (small n); the robust result is that ~22% of pitcher WAR change is role, and removing it moves the credit.
